steps.say: In a solid, the particles are packed in a pattern. In a liquid they are close but can slide. In a gas they are far apart and move freely. In a solution, the dissolved particles are mixed in with the liquid particles.
Many gases are invisible. At room temperature, common gases include oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide and hydrogen.
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius and melts at 0 degrees Celsius.
Water is unusual because it expands when it freezes. Ice takes up more space than the same mass of liquid water, so ice floats.
Water is also a good solvent: many substances dissolve in it.

check.prompt: At what temperature does pure water boil?
hints: It is the top of the usual thermometer.
Water at this temperature makes steam.

check.prompt: Which gas do plants take in from the air?

options.why: Helium is not taken in by plants.
Plants do not use nitrogen directly from the air.

hints: Plants make food in their leaves.
They take in a gas from the air.
check.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air.
